messages.subject: Stan and Xcode
parts:
Michael:

Thanks for your hints at how to use Xcode, which Andrew
forwarded to our developer's list (and to which I'm also
replying).

We use a mix of Mac, Windows and Linux, but none of us
know Xcode (we just use it to get the command-line tools,
which we then use scripted through make or through R; in
the intro, I wanted to actually explain the compile steps).

I'll give the GUI a whirl, and if it doesn't require
too much config, I'll add a note to the doc (with
thanks, of course).

> these data were recorded with too few decimal
> places so that the resulting quantization is clearly
> visible in a scatterplot.

For modeling the quantization error you mention, one
thing you can do is introduce a latent true location
and model the quantization process (for instance by restricting
the true location to an interval that would quantize to the
value you observe). That lets you jointly
infer the original data and use it inference. This is
the strategy outlined in Andrew's book(s) for censored
data, but the idea's the same.

- Bob
